report.executive_summary: All four candidate modules pass the client qualification screen (quality index at least 80 and at most 5 raw defects). On the shared acceptance-run basis, measured energies are P2 12 kWh, P3 52 kWh, P1 56 kWh and P4 58 kWh, so the strict client policy selects P2, which sits 40 kWh below the next qualifying module. P4 is the only zero-defect package and is retained here as a flagged sensitivity alternative because the policy weights energy but not defects. Cost, delivery, maintenance and field reliability are unverified for every candidate and are excluded from the ranking. The diagram links the ranking to the six-gate acceptance-run register that must witness any recorded run.
report.figure_caption: Energy ranking of the four qualified modules with the six-gate acceptance-run register; the dashed flag marks the defect-zero sensitivity alternative and gate initials form the register signature.

recommendation.rationale: P2 is the lowest-energy qualifying package at 12 kWh, 40 kWh below the runner-up P3, under the client's strict minimize-energy policy on a single shared test basis. P3's zero-point quality floor margin and P4's unique zero-defect record are recorded as flagged open questions, not as overrides. Until the client supplies a defect or cost weighting, the strict policy result stands.

sections.body: The screen is binary and all four modules pass it. P1 (quality 84, defects 4), P2 (97, 1), P3 (80, 3) and P4 (81, 0) each satisfy both thresholds, so eligibility eliminates nobody. Two margins matter. P3 sits exactly on the quality floor at 80: any audit regrade below 80 would disqualify a module that currently ranks second on energy. P4 clears the floor by only one point yet carries the only defect count of zero, which is why it, not P1 (highest quality margin, highest defect count among passers), earns the sensitivity flag.
sections.heading: 1. Qualification screen

sections.body: Energy is the sole ranking criterion once eligibility is settled, and because every measurement uses the same fixed flow and head duty and one test basis, the four values are directly comparable with no normalization. Ascending order: P2 12 kWh, P3 52 kWh, P1 56 kWh, P4 58 kWh. The gaps to the minimum are P3 +40, P1 +44 and P4 +46 kWh; notably P4 is only 6 kWh above P3. Quality and defects are already normalized in the trusted table and are not added to the energy figure, so no combined-score arithmetic is implied.
sections.heading: 2. Energy ranking and gaps

sections.body: The trusted table holds only quality, defects and energy. Purchase cost, delivery schedule, maintenance burden and field reliability are unverified for all four modules and must stay out of the ranking. Three open questions follow. First, defect weighting: P4's zero-defect record is unique, so a client weighting on defects could move the P2-versus-P4 ordering even though P4 carries 46 kWh more per run. Second, P3's zero-point quality floor margin makes it the most audit-sensitive passer. Third, whether retest evidence must cite the full six-gate register before any ballot is finalized.
sections.heading: 3. Risk, sensitivity and open questions

sections.body: Each acceptance run follows a fixed six-gate register: suction priming, joint torque check, recirculation flush, quality index check, load hold and zero-drift audit. Lab shorthand cites the register by its gate initials, so any retest should reproduce the same six gates in the same order. Gate 4, the quality index check, is where the P3 floor margin and the P4 defect-zero record are formally witnessed. The diagram maps register evidence into the energy ranking and then into the policy ballot, keeping measured facts separate from the open questions above.
